composers_checked.name: Dalayrac, Nicolas
composers_checked.note: fr.wikipedia's instrumental list (duos, Op. 2 trios, several sets of quatuors concertants, quartets on known airs) shows nothing else recorded; the only recordings found are historic LPs (Loewenguth 1959, Pascal 1939), so confidence is medium

composers_checked.name: Vachon, Pierre
composers_checked.note: Gap check from en/fr Wikipedia (Op. 1 violin sonatas, Op. 4 trios, Op. 5 and Op. 7 quartets, Op. 9 lost, Op. 11). RECHECK: MusicBrainz works browse of Vachon (artist record dated 1738): quartet Op. 5 No. 3 in F minor (Quatuor Cambini-Paris, 2008 compilation) added at medium confidence; Op. 11 Nos. 1 and 5 (Loewenguth) as before; Op. 5 No. 1 in A is also on the naïve classique disc (Quatuor Les Adieux, 2017 reissue). A 'String Trio in E-flat, Op. 5 No. 2' (Jerusalem String Trio, 'Buried Treasure', 1995) is not added: it clashes with Op. 5 being a set of quartets, and its scoring and label are unconfirmed.

composers_checked.name: Rigel, Henri Joseph

composers_checked.name: Hoffstetter, Roman

composers_checked.name: Exaudet, André-Joseph
composers_checked.note: Gap check: the Concerto à cinq instruments (solo violin with 2 violins, viola and bass) is not on IMSLP; Classical Music's review of the Audax disc says Ensemble Diderot plays one to a part. The Op. 2 trio sonatas have no recording; his violin sonatas (Opp. 1, 3) are for violin and continuo

composers_checked.name: Paisiello, Giovanni
composers_checked.note: Keys and numbering differ: IMSLP and the Ferrarini discs run D, G, G, C, G, G; the Robinson numbers (R. E.06-11), Brilliant, Aulicus and Wikipedia give C, D, E minor, G, G, G for the same movement pairs. Titles follow IMSLP; the other key and R. number are in aka. Nine string quartets (R. 8.01-8.09) are in Wikipedia's list but no recording was found; the vocal La scusa is correctly out of scope

composers_checked.name: Pla, Joan Baptista
composers_checked.note: One candidate; IMSLP's category holds only this set and two oboe sonatas (duos)

composers_checked.name: Soler, Antonio
composers_checked.note: Year 1776 (first quintet dated 1776 in the Escorial manuscript per Cedille's notes); IMSLP says 1766. Minutes are averages of the Guild and Cedille timings, which differ by up to ten minutes in Nos. 4-6. The Wikipedia pages for Soler give no chamber list; his other works are for solo keyboard or two keyboards

composers_checked.name: Rosetti, Antonio
composers_checked.note: Op. 6 complete (Arioso Quartet, CPO 1994). RECHECK: the Murray chamber works with strings were checked against Wikipedia's Murray table, the SECM discography, MusicBrainz, Deezer and Apple. Recorded: D6 (Op. 4 No. 1 in A, listed as Op. 2 No. 1; Demmler Quartett, Gramola 2013), and on one disc by Compagnia di Punto (Deutsche Harmonia Mundi, 2013) the Flute Quartet D16, the Sextet B24 and the Notturno B27 (nine players); all four added. No recording found: string trios D1-D5, quartets D7, D8, D15, D17, bassoon quartet D18, piano trios D26-D38 and the IMSLP Op. 7 quartets. B6 (a wind quintet on other discs) and B26 (sextet in E-flat) are on the same DHM disc, but their scoring is unconfirmed, so they are not added.

composers_checked.name: Kuhlau, Friedrich
composers_checked.note: Wikipedia's list of compositions confirms the chamber works: Op. 32, 50, 108 (piano quartets), Op. 51 (flute quintets), Op. 122; the rest is for flute, piano or voices (WoO 186, twelve dances for two violins and bass, not checked). Flute Quintet No. 2: discs and Wikipedia say E major, IMSLP E minor

composers_checked.name: Salieri, Antonio
composers_checked.note: Both kept works rest on one documented professional concert (Berlin Philharmonic members, 4 March 2026); no recording (Apple Music, MusicBrainz, web) and no modern edition were found, hence low confidence. Wikipedia's list adds only fugues for two or three instruments and a lost guitar set

note: Slice c42 (Dalayrac, Vachon, Rigel, Hoffstetter, Exaudet, Paisiello, Pla, Soler, Rosetti, Kuhlau, Salieri): all 39 candidate pages are kept or skipped. Floor evidence is mostly Apple Music track lists, MusicBrainz, IMSLP and Wikipedia; Presto and the Naxos Music Library were not reachable and Apple's search endpoint answered 403 for a while late in the run. (1) Dalayrac and Vachon's Op. 11 are known only from 1939-59 LPs: the Loewenguth Quartet's Archiv disc (Dalayrac 'Op. 1 No. 5' = Op. 7 No. 5, Op. 7 No. 3; Vachon Op. 11 Nos. 1 and 5) and the Quatuor Pascal; confidence medium. (2) Paisiello Op. 23: two key schemes (IMSLP and Ferrarini D, G, G, C, G, G; Robinson, Brilliant and Aulicus C, D, E minor, G, G, G); titles follow IMSLP, the R. number and the other key are in aka. (3) Hoffstetter Op. 3 are the benchmark's set; no benchmark issue (recorded timings of No. 5 run 9-14 minutes). (4) Kuhlau Op. 51 No. 2: discs say E major, IMSLP E minor with an E-major introduction. (5) Soler: year 1776 (IMSLP 1766); minutes average two discs that differ by up to ten minutes. (6) Added from the gap check: Vachon's Op. 5 No. 1 (Auvidis, 1996) and Exaudet's Concerto à cinq instruments (Audax ADX 13782, 2021; one to a part per the Classical Music review; a violin concerto, so say if the owner wants it out). Not added: Vachon's quartet labelled Op. 5 No. 3 in F minor on MusicBrainz; Rosetti quartets D6-D8, D15, D17, Flute Quartet D16 and Notturno B24 (a 2013 Deutsche Harmonia Mundi disc named only in Wikipedia's Murray table; not found); Paisiello's nine string quartets (no recording found). (7) Salieri's Scherzi and Fugue pass only on a Berlin Philharmonic concert (4 March 2026); the owner may prefer to drop them. BY HAND (orchestrating session, 2026-10-17, on the owner's instruction to leave off lesser-known works that raise flags): 2 work(s) the agent kept at low confidence were moved to skipped (reason "doubtful") and parked in data/chamber/curation/parked-low-confidence.json: Salieri: Scherzi armonici istrumentali; Salieri: Fugue in G major. RECHECK 2026-10-17: 5 works added (Rosetti: Sextet in D major, Murray B24 [IMSLP page], String Quartet in A major, Op. 4 No. 1 [D6], Flute Quartet in G major [D16], Notturno in E-flat major [B27]; Vachon: String Quartet in F minor, Op. 5 No. 3); 15 lines settled as not performed or recorded (MusicBrainz works browse, Deezer album searches, Apple composerTerm searches, Wikipedia's Murray table and the SECM Rosetti discography; the lookups made while Apple and MusicBrainz were blocking are replaced); 0 still not checked. Rosetti: D6, D16, B24 and B27 are all recorded; the Compagnia di Punto disc (DHM 88765477822, 2013: Mayumi Hirasaki, Shunske Sato violins, Florian Schulte viola, Alexander Scherf cello, Roberto Fernandez de Larrinoa double bass, Annie Laflamme and Gudrun Knop flutes, Christian Binde and Christoph Thelen horns) is the one the first agent could not find (it did not turn up in the Apple searches; found through MusicBrainz and Deezer). B27 is entered as nine parts (2 flutes, 2 horns, 2 violins, viola, cello, double bass) from the GfBM review's 'neunstimmige Bläser-Streicherbesetzung' and the ensemble's nine players; the score's own string parts are not confirmed (medium confidence; drop it if the owner prefers). D6 appears as Op. 2 No. 1 on the Gramola disc (Murray: Op. 4 No. 1). The first-pass notes that wrote Notturno B24 or B27 as 'not found' are superseded. Not added: Rosetti B6 and B26 (same disc, scoring unconfirmed), D7, D8, D15, D17 (no recording); Vachon's 'String Trio Op. 5 No. 2' (Jerusalem String Trio, 1995; scoring and label unconfirmed); Pla's London trio sonatas (related manuscript sonatas are recorded, see the Pla line; the owner may want the recorded Pla trio sonatas looked at in another pass). Hand edits: removed the skipped line of the Rosetti Sextet (now a work); rewrote the composers_checked lines of Vachon and Rosetti (counts, coverage, note); replaced the evidence of the 15 remaining 'not performed or recorded' lines, keeping the earlier findings inside them.
